entries.topic: Where the arrival conversation plays, and its timer
originals: Where does the arrival conversation play?
The arrival conversation (§4, §8 Q1)?
The arrival conversation (“Who are you?”, TRAIL / ANDROID / …)?
entries.answer: The template ends Jericho on Simon's 'Welcome to Jericho.' and opens Time to Decide ('In Jericho', PM 05:13) with 'Who are you?' and the prompts TRAIL / ANDROID / JERICHO / REFUGE / FREE? then LOST / SOMBER / LUCID / DIRECT; the strings are keyed X0503M (asset code), and only the second prompt has a timeout key (CHOICE02.TIMEOUT = TIME OUT). Benchmark builds both prompts in Time to Decide (MTD2, MTD3) after MJ14o's 'Welcome to Jericho.' The silent TIME OUT on the second prompt is not offered; it has no line, arrow or gate, so nothing needs fixing (timer length is in no source).
entries.source: template ch14 '## Finding Jericho' and ch16 '# In Jericho'; en.json X0503M.JERICHO.ENCOUNTER.PC.CHOICE01.* / CHOICE02.* incl. CHOICE02.TIMEOUT, X05MSIMON.WELCOME.1

entries.topic: Linear chapter: no prompt, risk, failure node or arrow (jumps, climb, door, magazine, bodies)
originals: No choice, no risk and no stat change: the chapter’s template has no?
No risk and no stat change?
Do a wall jump to cross over to the other side.” The wall?
The climb has no failure branch and carries no risk?
A deliberate, scripted jump that always lands safely (“You will have landed safely?
The door control is an input hurdle with no failure branch, so no?
Can any jump fail?
Can any jump (the gap, the ladder, the crane) fail, and what happens?
No public-opinion effect: no source gives one?
No source describes the body further or gives it an effect?
entries.answer: The chart is a single line to MET PEOPLE OF JERICHO with optional dead-end side nodes and no failure or death node; the 29 flowchart strings contain no fall or failure label; the template has no prompt, clue or arrow; PowerPyx says the crane jump lands 'safely in water'. A missed input can at most be retried, so there is nothing to model. Benchmark has no risk and no stat change anywhere in ch14.
entries.source: flowchart image jericho-100-flowchart-1.jpg (linear, one ending); en.json MENU.FLOWCHART.05M.* (no failure labels); template ch14 (no PROMPT/ARROW); PowerPyx 'Climb Crane and Jump … You will have landed safely'

entries.question: In a run where Connor stood still and Kara & Alice VANISHED in On the Run, which cover was on the Ferndale bench in Jericho: 'Android on the Run!' or 'Fortune Teller'?
entries.why: wiki Android_on_the_Run! line 36: 'Only appears if Kara and Alice were pursued by Connor'; PowerPyx text: 'she was seen by police and ran across the highway'; PowerPyx reader Hadley (2023-09-12, asks for confirmation) puts VANISHED and DIED ON THE HIGHWAY under Fortune Teller. The same flag drives Zlatko's chase report (public opinion down), so the answer also fixes an arrow. Benchmark: any pursuit sets chase → Android on the Run!. The died case needs no answer for Zlatko (Kara's story is over) and only changes a magazine cover.
